title: Candidate coaching plan and post-loop notes - Irene Novak
content:
Context:
This is a scratchpad for turning the interview loop feedback into an actionable candidate coaching / integration plan. Candidate finished loop 2025-11-01; panel was mixed-positive. Hiring manager asked for a write-up that could both: (a) surface risks we could mitigate with onboarding, and (b) be used if we extend an offer to set expectations and a support structure.

Quick summary (one-liner):
- Strong systems intuition + good latency/throughput mental models; weaker signals on cross-team communication and product tradeoff storytelling. Likely high-impact IC with ramp risk in stakeholder management.

Notes to self / raw impressions:
- Interviewer A (Marcus): liked architecture tradeoffs, flagged "tends to assume ideal infra" (no explicit follow-through on anti-fragile ops).
- Interviewer B (Aisha): good debugging demo, asked for clearer examples of prior on-call ownership and escalation.
- Interviewer C: worried about sync-cadence alignment (prefers cross-team docs).
- Candidate is enthusiastic about Redwood's mission; asked thoughtful Qs about Dedicated and Private offerings.

Open questions to resolve with HM (ask @Marcus):
- Does the role require running a cross-org postmortem program in first 6 months? If yes, add mentoring partner.
- Which team would own first-quarter deliverable? (Serving runtime vs infra)
- Compensation band preference and urgency on start date?

Risk buckets and mitigation ideas:
1) Ramp / cross-team communication (moderate risk)
   - Mitigation: 1:1s with product and SRE for first 8 weeks, assigned onboarding buddy from solutions-eng for cross-cust projects, explicit communication OKRs (first 90d: write two cross-team design docs).
2) Production hardening mindset (low-moderate)
   - Mitigation: pair on two incidents with senior SRE in weeks 2–6; include dedicated paging shadow shifts (no solo paging first 12 weeks).
3) Ambiguity around product tradeoffs (low)
   - Mitigation: workshop series with product manager on tradeoff framing; provide previous RFCs as examples.

Suggested 90-day plan (draft to share with HM and candidate if we extend):
- Week 0 (offer acceptance to start): send reading list and internal runbooks; schedule intro syncs.
- Weeks 1–4: orientation, infra and runtime deep-dives, pair debugging sessions, shadow SRE paging. Deliverable: short doc summarizing three latency/cost tradeoffs for a small feature.
- Weeks 5–12: take ownership of an end-to-end experiment (perf tuning or caching config), lead a cross-team design review. Deliverable: design + rollout plan and postmortem template.
- Weeks 13–24: handoff to steady-state, own small roadmap item, mentor an intern or junior engineer.

Concrete onboarding tasks (first two months):
- Read: internal perf playbook, serving-runtime architectural overview, incident postmortem index.
- Hands-on: repro a current perf regression in staging and write a notes summary.
- Communication: present 15-min "what I learned" in eng-all after month 1.

Hiring committee artifacts to prepare if moving forward:
- Proposed offer packet with base + RSU outline (get bands from comp team).
- Two reference checks: (1) prior manager on conflict resolution; (2) peer on cross-team collaboration.
- Mentorship pledge: primary mentor = Senior Staff SRE; secondary buddy = Solutions Eng.

Draft candidate-facing paragraph (for initial outreach if offer):
"We appreciated how you approached system-level tradeoffs and debugging during the loop. We see a clear path for you to impact our serving runtime performance quickly. To set you up for success we plan a structured first 90 days with dedicated cross-team pairing, incident shadowing, and a short deliverable you can own to demonstrate impact. If that aligns with your expectations, I can share a formal offer and the onboarding plan."

Loose checklist before we close loop:
- [ ] Confirm HM alignment on 90-day ownership item
- [ ] Get comp band and draft offer language from comp ops
- [ ] Book reference calls
- [ ] Draft mentorship & buddy calendar
- [ ] One-pager for candidate that includes FAQ on Dedicated vs Private infra (candidate asked specifics)

Misc notes and artifacts to copy into Confluence (put under hiring/engineer-onboarding/candidate-<last>-plan):
- raw panel quotes (keep anonymous), 90-day plan, risk mitigation list, suggested mentors, reference questions.

Low-effort next steps (today):
1) ping Marcus in Slack w/ this doc and ask the three questions under "open questions"
2) DM comp-ops for band range (include title: Senior Runtime Engineer)
3) schedule 30-min sync with Aisha to capture specific examples to include in the candidate-facing summary

Notes to self: keep this informal — candidate is still in decision phase; avoid heavy legal language in early message. Keep timeline tight: aim to have offer draft + ref checks scheduled within 5 business days of HM sign-off.

End of notes.
